rie: Automated EEG-based epilepsy discrimination has been studied extensively, but most approaches rely on multichannel recordings acquired under controlled conditions, limiting applicability to wearable monitoring during daily activities. This study presents an activity-aware discrimination framework using portable single-channel EEG acquired from the frontopolar (FP1) position during activities of daily living (ADL). The pipeline combines short-window segmentation, maximal overlap discrete wavelet transform multiresolution analysis (MODWT-MRA), and interpretable handcrafted amplitude, temporal-variation, nonlinear-energy, entropy, and spectral features. The framework is evaluated on 90 recordings (60 healthy, 30 epileptic) under four settings: combined, stationary, light ambulatory, and intense ambulatory. The selected configuration uses 5 s windows with 50% overlap and an ensemble classifier. Under leave-one-recording-out (LORO) validation with nested Bayesian hyperparameter selection, the primary evaluation, the ensemble achieves accuracies of 80.00%, 79.15%, 84.79%, and 85.71%, with balanced accuracies of 73.43–83.87% and sensitivities of 57.14–79.76%. Nested segmentlevel 10-fold cross-validation, a within-recording estimate, yields 89.37%, 88.42%, 94.47%, and 93.51%. Under LORO, MODWT-MRA features give the ensemble higher accuracy than raw-segment features in every setting and than decimated-wavelet features in the stationary and intense ambulatory settings, and the complete pipeline requires approximately 20–115 ms per 5 s segment on a laptop processor. These results establish recording-level generalization only and provide a proof of concept for epilepsy/healthy cohort discrimination using wearable single-channel EEG.
bspc: Wearable single-channel EEG is increasingly used to monitor epileptic patients outside the clinic, but the physical activity of daily living (ADL) continuously shapes the recorded signal. This activity-coupled variability is typically discarded as noise, even though it holds recoverable contextual information. Until now, EEG-based human activity recognition (HAR) has been studied almost exclusively in healthy participants under controlled lab conditions, leaving ADL recognition in clinical epileptic populations unaddressed. This study introduces a single-channel frontal EEG framework for ADL recognition, evaluated jointly on healthy, epileptic, and combined cohorts. As ambulatory EEG is multicomponent and nonstationary, a five-level maximal overlap discrete wavelet transform-multiresolution analysis (MODWT-MRA) with the Coiflet-3 wavelet decomposes each epoch into five frequency-resolved detail components, from which a compact 55-dimensional handcrafted descriptor is extracted and classified using an ensemble learner. Two recognition granularities are considered: a three-class intensity scheme (stationary, light ambulatory, intense ambulatory) and a fine-grained eight-class individual-ADL scheme, tested across multiple temporal window lengths. Using class-balanced, recording-level holdout evaluation, the framework achieves three-state activity recognition accuracies of 79.7%, 89%, and 85.2% for the Healthy, Epileptic, and Combined cohorts, respectively, with the 5-second window consistently delivering strong performance across all three groups. The method is further tested on the eight harmonized individual ADLs, offering additional insight at the activity-specific level. To our knowledge, this is the first framework to jointly perform EEG-based ADL recognition in both healthy and clinical epileptic cohorts, extending single-channel activity profiling from controlled healthy settings to activity-aware wearable monitoring in clinical populations.
svmd: Accurate time-frequency (TF) analysis of the electrocardiogram (ECG) is vital for interpreting its beat-to-beat activity, yet its recurring waveforms make crossterm-free representation difficult. The Wigner–Ville distribution (WVD) offers the highest TF resolution among bilinear representations, but its quadratic nature generates inner and outer cross-terms that obscure the true energy of nonlinear and multi-component non-stationary signals. Variational mode decomposition (VMD) based methods reduce these terms but require the number of modes in advance and are sensitive to initialization, while whole-signal successive VMD (SVMD) cannot separate components that share a narrow band at different time instants. This paper proposes a short-term SVMD based WVD (ST-SVMD-WVD) that segments the signal with overlapping short-term windows, applies SVMD to each segment to obtain automatically selected band-limited modes, and combines their WVDs with an overlap-compensating energy-scaling step. The short-term segmentation isolates same-band components occurring at different times and linearizes nonlinear instantaneous-frequency laws within each window, while SVMD removes the need to preset the number of modes and is robust to initialization. The method is tested on two synthetic signals, a normal sinus rhythm ECG under clean and noisy conditions (5, 10, and 15 dB), and four arrhythmia classes from the MIT-BIH database, and is compared with five reference methods using four TF measures. ST-SVMD-WVD gives the best result on all four measures for both synthetic signals. On the ECG signals it gives the lowest normalized Rényi entropy and highest energy concentration in all normal-rhythm cases and in three of the four arrhythmia classes. Some reference methods score better on the Stankovi´c measure or ratio of norms in some normal-rhythm cases, but their TFRs show scattered or blurred components, whereas ST-SVMD-WVD shows one compact component at each beat on a clean background.
imummg: Natural and reliable hand gesture recognition is becoming a key enabler for intuitive human-computer interaction in internet of things (IoT) environments, especially for wearable and assistive systems where camera-based sensing is unsuitable. This paper presents an inertial measurement unit (IMU) based framework that converts raw tri-axial accelerometer and gyroscope signals into structured time-frequency images and classifies them using a lightweight convolutional network. First, we propose a stackingbased multivariate time-frequency representation method termed TFR-StackGrid. In this method, the smoothed pseudo Wigner-Ville distribution (SPWVD) is computed for each of the six IMU-MMG channels. The resulting time-frequency maps are then systematically arranged into a fixed 2×3 kinematic grid. This structured configuration preserves the spatial relationship between translational acceleration and rotational motion, thereby integrating multivariate information into a single stacked time-frequency representation, referred to as S-TFR. A compact Gesture Net architecture is then designed to operate directly on these images, combining stacked 2D convolution blocks with a shallow classification head for 11 dynamic hand gesture classes. We conduct a comprehensive evaluation on the large-scale hand gesture accelerometer and gyroscope Dataset (HGAG-DATA), containing 11 gestures, 23,650 samples from 43 participants, and compare seven different time-frequency schemes, including wavelet and other quadratic distributions. The proposed SPWVD-based TFR-StackGrid with Gesture Net achieves 96.21% micro accuracy and 96.28% macro accuracy, with balanced per-class precision, recall, and F1scores, while relying only on a single wrist-worn IMU based mechanomyography signals. These results demonstrate that structured time-frequency imaging combined with a lightweight convolutional backbone can effectively mitigate the limitations of template matching, handcrafted feature pipelines, and heavier deep sequence models for practical IMU-MMG-based hand gesture recognition.
hatseq: Driver drowsiness represents a significant risk to road safety, being a major contributor to traffic accidents. This study introduces a hybrid adaptive temporal sequential network HatSeqNet, an effectively designed architecture for cross-subject driver drowsiness detection using single-channel electroencephalogram (EEG) signals across different subjects. Leveraging the Mexican hat wavelet (MHW) transform, EEG signals are transformed into time-scale representations (TSRs), capturing intricate neural patterns and transient dynamics. These TSRs are processed by a hybrid convolutional neural network (CNN) and recurrent neural network (RNN) architecture, which effectively models spatial and temporal dependencies. The model is evaluated using leave-one-subject-out cross-validation (LOSO-CV) on a publicly available EEG dataset from a sustained-attention driving task. HatSeqNet achieves a state-of-the-art average accuracy of 88.26%, with precision, recall, and F1-score of 88.87%, 87.63%, and 88.10%, respectively. These metrics surpass those of prior studies on the same SAT dataset. The employment of single-channel EEG enhances the system’s portability, rendering HatSeqNet suitable for practical vehicular applications. The superior performance of the proposed architecture underscores its potential to enhance road safety through reliable and noninvasive driver drowsiness detection, even without personalized calibration.
sleep: Sleep posture transitions (SPTs) are critical indicators of sleep quality, essential for preventing posture-related complications in clinical and assistive care. Conventional vision-based, infrared, and pressure-mat monitoring systems face limitations in privacy preservation and robustness. This letter presents a sensor-oriented radar signal processing method for SPT recognition using frequency-modulated continuous-wave radar, processing time-range (TR) maps through a hierarchical temporal architecture. The proposed single-branch network employs depthwise convolutions, multihead self-attention, generalized mean pooling, and bidirectional recurrent modeling to extract discriminative features from radar-signal-derived TR representations. Evaluated on a seven-class SPT dataset with 1407 TR samples from 20 participants, the method achieves 99.29% accuracy under fivefold cross-validation. A subject-independent leave-one-subject-out evaluation further confirms strong generalization, with performance of 99.22% ± 1.78% across subjects. Robustness analysis under Gaussian noise perturbation maintains 98.94% accuracy, indicating resilience to signal degradation and environmental variations. Comparative analysis with time-Doppler maps with 1400 samples achieves 95.71% accuracy, demonstrating the superiority of range-based displacement representations over velocity-based signatures. The compact 18.6 M parameter architecture with 2.10 giga floating point operations per second and 5.787 ms inference time enables real-time deployment in privacy-preserving healthcare monitoring systems while maintaining sensor-level signal fidelity.
alu_j: Energy-efficient and high-speed arithmetic units are fundamental building blocks in resource-constrained systems, including Internet of Things (IoT) devices and embedded processors. This requirement necessitates the development of Arithmetic Logic Units (ALUs) optimized in terms of power consumption, silicon area, and performance in advanced nanoscale technologies. In this work, the design and comparative analysis of two 8-bit, 12-function ALUs implemented using Transmission Gate (TG) logic and NMOS Pass Transistor Logic (N-Pass) are presented using Cadence Virtuoso with GPDK 90 nm technology. The proposed architectures support a wide range of operations, such as addition, subtraction, multiplication, bitwise shifting, and parity generation. The performance is evaluated based on critical parameters, including propagation delay, power consumption, operating frequency, and transistor count. Simulation results at a supply voltage of 1.8 V indicate that the TG-based ALU achieves superior speed performance, exhibiting a propagation delay of 0.1655 ns and an operating frequency of 58.9 MHz, making it suitable for high-performance computing applications such as microprocessors. Conversely, the N-Pass-based ALU demonstrates improved power efficiency, with an average power consumption of 0.19275 W and power dissipation of 1.67 mW, which are favorable for low-power IoT applications. The comparative analysis highlights the inherent design trade-offs, revealing a 99.76% reduction in delay for the TG implementation and a 98.36% reduction in power dissipation for the N-Pass design, thereby providing valuable insights for selecting appropriate logic styles in application-specific integrated circuit design.
gamma: Cognitive load classification is a crucial task for understanding mental effort during cognitively demanding activities and for enabling efficient EEGbased monitoring systems. This paper presents a lightweight approach for multi-level cognitive load classification using gamma band filtered EEG features and classical machine learning models. The proposed framework extracts compact statistical, energy-based, and temporal descriptors from non-overlapping 2s gamma-band EEG segments and reduces computational complexity by focusing on task-relevant spectral content. Feature relevance is optimized, and three widely used classifiers, decision trees, k-nearest neighbors, and ensemble-based models are evaluated using Bayesian hyperparameter optimization and 10-fold crossvalidation. Experimental results demonstrate that the optimized ensemble classifier achieves the highest accuracy of 98.52% for the mental arithmetic task and 98.40% for the Stroop Color Word Task. The framework is validated on EEG data collected from 15 participants using an 8-channel OpenBCI system and provides a practical, resource-efficient solution for real-time, lowchannel cognitive load monitoring. The results highlight the effectiveness of gamma-centric statistical features over more computationally intensive approaches, offering a favorable balance between accuracy and efficiency.
sethar: Radar-based human activity recognition (HAR) offers noncontact sensing, environmental robustness, and privacy preservation, but its performance is limited by the quality of nonstationary micro-Doppler signatures in frequency-modulated continuous-wave (FMCW) radar signals. Conventional time–frequency methods, such as short-time Fourier transform and Wigner–Ville distribution, suffer from spectral blurring and cross-term interference, reducing sensing resolution. This letter introduces an improved sensor-oriented time–frequency enhancement framework for FMCW radar HAR using the synchroextracting transform (SET), which selectively extracts energy along instantaneous frequency ridges to suppress some artifacts and enhance micro-Doppler concentration. Applied to clutter-suppressed slow-time signals, SET produces highly concentrated and interpretable time– frequency representations (TFRs), directly improving radar sensing fidelity. The proposed approach is evaluated on the NJUST FMCW radar dataset, where SET-derived TFRs show improved concentration and activity separability over conventional methods. Using a lightweight time–frequency anisotropic radar network, the framework achieves 98.71% accuracy and a 96.14% F1-score with low computational cost (0.119 s per sample), demonstrating that sensor-level time–frequency enhancement leads to measurable gains in FMCW radar HAR systems for improved sensor-based performance.
cough: Cough classification is a crucial task for early diagnosis of respiratory diseases such as pneumonia and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. This paper presents a novel approach for classifying wet and dry coughs using power spectrum features and classical machine learning models. The proposed framework extracts statistical descriptors from segmented cough signals and addresses class imbalance using the synthetic minority over-sampling technique. Four widely used classifiers—support vector machines (SVM), k-nearest neighbors, decision trees, and ensemble methods—are evaluated across different dataset configurations and segmentation schemes. Experimental results demonstrate that SVM, when combined with 16-segment features, achieves the highest classification accuracy of 93.67%. The framework is validated on a dataset of 1,908 cough recordings and offers a practical, resource-efficient solution for real-time, resource-constrained applications in early disease detection and telemedicine. The results highlight the effectiveness of statistical features over deep learning approaches, offering a balance between accuracy and computational efficiency.
pid: Reliable voltage regulation is essential for ensuring the stability and resilience of modern power systems under dynamic load variations and disturbances. This paper presents a unified comparative framework for evaluating Automatic Voltage Regulator (AVR) performance using classical controllers, regression-based models, and a Neural Network (NN)–enhanced PID controller implemented in MATLAB/Simulink. The framework includes PID, PI, PD, P, I, and PIDA controllers alongside linear and ensemble regression models with the proposed NN-PID serving as the primary enhancement. Controller performance was assessed using statistical and time-domain metrics. The NN-PID achieved zero overshoot, a settling time of 2.93 s, and a coefficient of determination of 0.9998, outperforming the baseline PID, which exhibited 4.43% overshoot, a 4.28 s settling time, and a coefficient of determination of 0.9759. Linear regression achieved the fastest rise time of 0.27 s with near-perfect accuracy of 0.9999 but showed limited robustness under nonlinear dynamics, while ensemble models delivered stable but slower responses. The NN-PID achieved a superior balance of accuracy, robustness, and adaptability compared with recent optimization-driven PID variants. The results emphasize the novelty and practical importance of integrating machine learning into AVR controller design to strengthen the reliability and adaptability of power systems.
gcaf: The classification of rare and endangered medicinal plants is an urgent necessity in Bangladesh and ecologically similar regions to safeguard biodiversity and conserve traditional medical practices. However, contemporary methodologies are constrained by limited available data and a lack of accurate and interpretable deep learning frameworks. To address these challenges, an advanced convolutional neural network (CNN)- based deep learning architecture named GCAF-Net has been proposed in this paper to identify rare and endangered medicinal plants in Bangladesh. The framework has been designed to combine EfficientNetV2 for feature extraction, a spatial attention mechanism for enhanced feature learning, and Grad-CAM for generating explainable predictions along with a custom CNN model to predict the results. Both global and local features are integrated to achieve improved accuracy. The proposed framework has achieved a macro accuracy of 99.80% and a micro accuracy of 99.71% for the Rare and Endangered Medicinal Plant dataset, establishing new performance standards. The robust performance of the proposed framework is expected to contribute significantly in biodiversity conservation efforts.
alu_c: In contemporary digital systems, the Arithmetic Logic Unit is a critical component for optimizing both performance and power efficiency. This paper introduces a novel, miniaturized 8-bit ALU with 12 functions, implemented using Transmission Gate logic in 90nm CMOS technology. The design incorporates addition/subtraction, shift operations, multiplication, increment/decrement, parity checking, comparison, binary to gray conversion, and 2’s complement. Implemented in Cadence Virtuoso using the gpdk 90nm library, the ALU achieves a low propagation delay of 0.172 ns and power consumption of 102 mW, yielding a power-delay product of 1.7544×10−11 J. Compared to traditional CMOS implementations, our TG-based architecture reduces transistor count by 47.3% and offers improved speed and energy efficiency. Its architecture, governed by a 3-bit control mechanism, provides both flexibility and adaptability, making it suitable for applications requiring high performance as well as those prioritizing minimal energy usage.
vox: Extreme vocal distortion techniques are a defining element of heavy metal performance, yet their computational analysis remains relatively underexplored, particularly for finegrained discrimination among acoustically similar harsh-vocal styles. This paper presents a practical analysis pipeline for extreme vocal distortion techniques using the Extreme Metal Vocals Dataset (EMVD). The study focuses on four principal classes and combines structured signal preprocessing, handcrafted acoustic feature extraction, singer-independent evaluation, and deployment-oriented recording-level inference. To reflect both controlled and realistic vocal conditions, separate pipelines are developed for vowel-based and lyric-based recordings, and Random Forest, Support Vector Machine (SVM), and AdaBoost.M2 are compared under singer-level partitioning. In singer-independent testing, the best vowel-based result achieved 89.74% accuracy, while the best lyric-based result achieved 87.21% accuracy. However, recording-level analysis showed that SVM produced more stable and acoustically plausible segmentwise behavior, making it the most suitable backend for deployment. These results show that practical extreme-vocal analysis benefits from evaluation beyond benchmark scores alone and can be supported by an interpretable acoustic pipeline for more realistic recording-level use.
form: Poor technique in resistance training is a leading cause of musculoskeletal injury, and the risk grows within a set as accumulating fatigue erodes movement control. We propose FormSense, a wrist-worn six-degree-of-freedom inertial measurement unit (IMU) application that closes three gaps in existing wearable systems: inability to localise a fault within a single repetition, dependence on large supervised datasets, and the absence of an actionable link between within-set form decline and fatigue. A 100 Hz signal stream is reduced to orientationinvariant magnitudes, segmented and resampled into fixed-length repetitions, and compared against an expert-derived reference template built from four expert athletes. Every repetition is partitioned into three biomechanical phases (initiation, main drive, deceleration) and graded GOOD, AVERAGE, or BAD using percentile thresholds drawn from the expert distribution; a plain-English diagnostic engine attributes each weak phase to insufficient peak force, acceleration-path mismatch, or inconsistent wrist rotation, and a fatigue and consistency layer flags withinset decline and recommends load reduction. Validated across five exercises, FormSense produced phase-level correlations of r = 0.20 to 0.87 for experts and r = −0.30 to 0.70 for the novice, delivering real-time per-repetition feedback for technique correction and injury prevention without laboratory equipment.
